title: Normal schemes with Noetherian underlying space have open integral components
statement: Let $Z$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] whose underlying topological space is Noetherian, meaning that every descending chain of closed subsets stabilizes. Suppose $Z$ is normal: for every $z\in Z$, the local ring $\mathcal O_{Z,z}$ is an integral domain integrally closed in its fraction field [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring]. Then $Z$ has finitely many irreducible components [def-weil-irreducible-components]; they are pairwise disjoint open and closed subsets, and with their open subscheme structures they are normal integral schemes [def-pc-integral-scheme]. The empty scheme is allowed, with zero components. No local Noetherian condition on the structure sheaf is assumed.

source.place: Tag 0357, lemma-normal-locally-finite-nr-irreducibles; the finiteness condition for every quasi-compact open follows from Tag 0052, topology.tex, lemma-Noetherian (1)--(2).

proof.text: The NoetherianSpace theorem finite_irreducibleComponents gives finiteness of the components of Z, using only the underlying topology.

For x in Z, the set S_x of generizations of x is the image of Spec(O_{Z,x}) under the canonical morphism: Mathlib Scheme.range_fromSpecStalk is precisely the image clause of lem-weil-pbc-spec-local-ring-canonical-morphism. This spectrum is irreducible since its ring is a domain. Continuous images and closure preserve irreducibility, so closure(S_x) is irreducible. If C is a component containing x, choose a generic point eta of C (schemes are quasi-sober). Then eta specializes to x, hence eta belongs to S_x and C=closure{eta} is contained in closure(S_x). Maximality of C forces C=closure(S_x). This is the generization argument used in WeilConjectures.Mathlib.AlgebraicGeometry.Noetherian.irreducibleSpace_of_isDomain_stalk, applied directly to global components; it needs no algebraic Noetherian hypothesis.

Two components containing x both equal closure(S_x), so distinct components are disjoint. For a component C, every point outside C lies in another component, while disjointness excludes points of C from any other component. Thus C is the complement of the union of all other components. This is a finite union of closed sets, so C is open; component maximality already gives closedness. No point or component is selected from the empty scheme, so this also handles the empty case.

Give C its open subscheme structure U. The open immersion U -> Z induces an isomorphism on stalk rings. Transport IsDomain and IsIntegrallyClosed across its ring equivalence. Domain stalks imply U is reduced (isReduced_of_isReduced_stalk). The irreducibility of C gives IrreducibleSpace U by isIrreducible_iff_irreducibleSpace. Therefore U is integral by isIntegral_of_irreducibleSpace_of_isReduced. All constructions and conclusions retain the original statement and universes.

Sources: Stacks 0357 (properties.tex l.933) and 030C (algebra.tex l.8275), plus the tags for 0052, 00ES, 01HV, 01HF and 01ON. The statement is true and is a correct form of 0357 with |Z| topologically Noetherian, which gives 0357's finiteness on quasi-compact opens. It never assumes the ring is Noetherian, so it is not a duplicate of the Noetherian results rem-pc-regular-normal(2) (033M), lem-sbc-normal-sections-finite-product or lem-a1-normal-etale-components-clopen. Tested on: the empty scheme, Spec of a normal domain, Spec(A×B), a rank-1 non-discrete valuation ring, and xy=0, which is excluded and shows normality is needed. Steps: S2 gets finitely many minimal primes via the injective map q↦V(q). S3 gets reducedness from the equivalence written in def-pc-reduced-scheme and normality from the localization clause (c) of affine-open-stalk-localization. S4 applies 030C (1)⇒(3) with its hypotheses checked. S5 is a correct idempotent calculation: K_i minimal, V(K_i)=D(e_i), n=0 handled. S6–S7 do the open-subspace correspondence and the gluing (open, disjoint, covering, finite). S8 uses unchanged stalks on the open subscheme and the integral-scheme equivalence. proof_deps equals the union of uses, there is no cycle and no SGA. lean.statement: theorem normal_topologicallyNoetherian_components (Z : Scheme.{u}) [TopologicalSpace.NoetherianSpace Z] (hnormal : ∀ z : Z, IsDomain (Z.presheaf.stalk z) ∧ IsIntegrallyClosed (Z.presheaf.stalk z)) : (irreducibleComponents Z).Finite ∧ (irreducibleComponents Z).Pairwise Disjoint ∧ ∀ C ∈ irreducibleComponents Z, ∃ hC : IsOpen C, IsClosed C ∧ IsIntegral (Scheme.Opens.toScheme (⟨C, hC⟩ : Z.Opens)) ∧ ∀ z : (Scheme.Opens.toScheme (⟨C, hC⟩ : Z.Opens)), IsDomain ((Scheme.Opens.toScheme (⟨C, hC⟩ : Z.Opens)).presheaf.stalk z) ∧ IsIntegrallyClosed ((Scheme.Opens.toScheme (⟨C, hC⟩ : Z.Opens)).presheaf.stalk z)
